{"relevant": true, "severity": "critical", "message": "internal/media/avatar.go POST /avatar: saving under ./uploads with the client-provided filename allows path traversal (filename like `../../etc/x` or `../main.go` overwrites arbitrary files) and lets attackers overwrite other users' avatars or upload `.html`/`.svg` for stored XSS. Fix: ignore the client name and generate a server-side name (uuid + extension from an allowlist, e.g. .png/.jpg/.webp), build the path with filepath.Join on a fixed dir, and verify the result stays inside it. Also wrap the body in http.MaxBytesReader (e.g. 2MB), sniff the type with http.DetectContentType rather than trusting Content-Type, and require an authenticated user so the avatar is tied to their ID. Serve uploads with `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and preferably from a separate origin or non-executable path."}
